title: Introduce presubmit cost quotas and dependency categorizer
author: Aisha N. Patel
release_notes: Adds presubmit CI spend quotas, a lightweight dependency categorizer used by dep-bot to prioritize updates, and a rollout plan for canary and org-wide enablement. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Presubmit CI spend has been growing steadily as more teams enable full integration suites on every PR. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a configurable presubmit cost quota system that estimates the expected CI spend per PR and enforces a soft quota to reduce wastey runs, and (2) a dependency categorizer service that tags third-party dependencies as stable, frequent, or volatile to inform dep-bot behavior and presubmit test selection. Changes are aimed at reducing CI cost (SLO: 20% reduction in unnecessary longtest runs) while keeping fast feedback for developers.
Design summary:
- Presubmit cost quota: a lightweight estimator (runner-second + cache-miss heuristic) attached to the presubmit planner. We compute an "estimated_ci_units" per PR at intake and surface it in the GitHub checks summary. Repos can specify per-team default quotas in .ci/config.yaml and override per-branch. If a PR exceeds the quota, the presubmit runner demotes long, non-blocking tests to a deferred lane and annotates the PR with quota details and a link to request a one-time quota bump.
- Dependency categorizer: a small service and build-time classifier that samples manifest changes (package.json / go.mod / pyproject.toml) across the monorepo and historical update frequency + CVE signals to assign categories: stable (rare updates, low churn), frequent (regular updates, active maintainers), volatile (rapid releases or high-security churn). Dep-bot uses the category to schedule automatic patch updates for stable deps, prioritized review for volatile, and aggregated rollups for frequent.
Implementation highlights:
- New presubmit estimator module (golang) integrated into the presubmit orchestrator and the GitHub composite action.
- .ci/config.yaml schema extended with 'presubmit_quota_units' and 'quota_behavior' (soft_warn, demote_longtests, block). Default: soft_warn.
- Dependency categorizer service (python) with a lightweight SQLite cache for signals (we avoided heavy infra to simplify rollout).
- Dep-bot adaptation: changes to the dependency update scheduling module so it reads categorizer labels and uses an updated backoff strategy.
- UI: GitHub check summary and a small presubmit-cost badge in the PR header.
Testing & rollout:
- Unit tests for estimator and categorizer added; integration tests run in the harness.
- Canary rollout to the "perf-canary" org for 48 hours: we ran ~250 PRs, observed a 24% reduction in longtest executions for PRs flagged over quota.
- Gradual enablement via feature flag: default off for teams; enable by setting .ci/config.yaml.
- Rollback path: feature flag off and revert presubmit planner config; quick patch to remove estimator if issues observed.
CI and checks:
- All CI checks passed in the canary runs (lint, unit, presubmit-sim, smoke-run).
- We added a short CI job "ci/quota-smoke" that validates estimator outputs for changed paths on PRs.
Migration notes:
- Teams with bespoke presubmit wiring will need to add the estimator shim (two-line change).
- Dep-bot config has a new optional field 'categorizer_policy' for teams that want to opt out.
Related work: ENG-1543 (presubmit-costs initiative), PM-987 (dep-bot prioritization).
Commands to exercise locally:
- make presubmit-estimate PATH=path/to/changed/files
- python tools/dep_categorizer/run.py --sample 100
Operational runbook (short):
- If estimator spikes unexpectedly, set override in .ci/config.yaml to avoid demotion, investigate via /ops/ci-quota-traces.
- Categorizer health: ensure sqlite cache not corrupted; small repair tool included.
Why this is different: prior PRs focused on CI job sharding, caching, and presubmit fastpaths. This PR ties explicit cost estimation to gating decisions and pairs it with dependency signals to make automated updates less noisy.
